title: fix(mcp): refuse undeclared argument keys on every MCP tool instead of stripping them
body:
Closes #16913

`query_records` answered an unsupported sort key with `200` and rows in seed order, and an
unsupported filter key with `200` and the full unfiltered set. Both keys were undeclared, and both
were deleted before the handler ran. This PR refuses them, on every tool, with a message that names
the key and the spelling to send instead.

## Where each refusal actually lives — measured, not recalled

The card is right that one tool holds two postures, but the two mechanisms are **not in the same
package**, and that turns out to be the whole reason the split existed.

| refusal | lives at | judged against |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| the `fields` refusal the card holds up as good behaviour | `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts:1340` (``Unknown field 'FIELD' on object 'OBJECT'``), plus `assertProjectionHasNoDottedPaths` around `:1029` | the object's real field map, one layer below MCP |
| the new undeclared-**argument-key** refusal | `packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts`, `strictToolInput()` | the tool's own declared argument shape |

`git grep "Unknown field '" -- packages/mcp/src` returns **zero** (positive control: the same
matcher returns 4 hits under `packages/objectql/src`). So from the caller's seat the tool did hold
two postures; inside this file it held exactly one, and it was the wrong one. Nothing about `fields`
changed here.

## The seam, and a premise it falsifies

`registerTool`'s `inputSchema` is typed `ZodRawShapeCompat | AnySchema` in
`@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 1.30.0 — it accepts a fully built schema, not only a raw shape. The
repo already recorded this: `toolInputSchema()` in `mcp-server-runtime.ts` cites the same reading.
So no seam had to be invented, and no handler ever needed to see the dropped keys.

Measured directly against the installed SDK, one tool per posture, same call:

```text
tools/call  {objectName: 'crm_opportunity', sort: '-amount'}
  raw shape    -> isError: false   handler received {"objectName":"crm_opportunity"}
  strict obj   -> isError: true    "Unrecognized key(s) ... Did you mean `sort` -> `orderBy`?"
tools/list inputSchema
  raw shape    -> ... "required":["objectName"]
  strict obj   -> ... "required":["objectName"],"additionalProperties":false
```

Two properties of that second row are the deliverable:

- the refusal arrives as a **tool error** (`isError: true`, text content), not as an exception
  across the wire — the SDK converts its own `McpError` through `createToolError()`, so this file's
  standing promise ("errors are returned as tool errors, never thrown across the wire") holds;
- `tools/list` renders `additionalProperties: false`, so an agent reads the narrowing off the
  schema instead of discovering it by being refused. Triage asked for the narrowing to be
  **declared**; that is where it is declared.

## The sweep — all eleven tools, and the twelfth registrar

`packages/mcp/src` has 12 `server.registerTool` sites. Read as matched lines, not counts:

| registrar | sites | posture before | posture now |
| :-- | :--: | :-- | :-- |
| `mcp-http-tools.ts` — the data + action tools | 11 | **silent strip, all eleven** | refused, key named, spelling suggested |
| `mcp-server-runtime.ts:1123` `registerToolFromDefinition` | 1 | honours the **author's** JSON Schema | unchanged, deliberately |
| `stdio-data-bridge.ts` | 0 | no registrar at all | unchanged |

The sweep's red-before is in the test file and is unambiguous — the assertion listed all eleven
tool names as accepting an undeclared key:

```text
AssertionError: expected [ 'list_objects', …(10) ] to deeply equal []
+ [ "list_objects", "describe_object", "validate_expression", "query_records",
+   "aggregate_records", "get_record", "create_record", "update_record",
+   "delete_record", "list_actions", "run_action" ]
```

So the split was not one tool disagreeing with itself — it was **eleven tools agreeing on the wrong
posture**, with the good posture living in another package.

**Why the twelfth site is not in scope, measured rather than judged.** It converts an
`AIToolDefinition.parameters` JSON Schema with `z.fromJSONSchema`, and that conversion preserves
the author's declaration in both directions:

```text
{type:'object', properties:{q:…}}                            -> parse ok, `zz` KEPT and passed to the handler
{type:'object', properties:{q:…}, additionalProperties:false} -> parse fails, `unrecognized_keys`
```

It never silently strips. An open schema passes the key through because JSON Schema's
`additionalProperties` defaults to true — that is the tool author's declared contract, faithfully
served. Closing it here would override an author's declaration, which is the opposite of what this
card asks for. `stdio-data-bridge.ts` contains no registrar at all (positive control:
`McpDataBridge` matches at `:4`, `:9`, `:92`; a fabricated path returns 0).

## Prior art — reused, not rebuilt

The repo already ruled on this disease and already owns the parts. `strictToolInput()` is two lines
over the published `strictUnknownKeyError` factory from `@objectstack/spec/shared`, which is
already carried in `packages/spec/api-surface/shared.json` — **no new export, no new machinery,
nothing added to any public surface**, and no edit to `packages/spec`.

Bare `.strict()` would not have been enough. Zod alone answers `Unrecognized key: "sort"`, which
tells an agent it was wrong and not what to write. What it answers now:

```text
Unrecognized key(s) on this query_records call: `sort`. Did you mean `sort` -> `orderBy`?
This argument used to be dropped silently and the call still succeeded, so a mis-guessed
parameter name answered a differently filtered or differently ordered set with no way for
the caller to tell.
```

(No tracker id in that sentence, deliberately: `pnpm check:doc-authoring` reds on one in runtime
string prose, because the readers of a tool error — an MCP client, an agent transcript, a log —
cannot resolve it. The anchor sits in an adjacent comment instead. That gate caught this branch and
is the one red the sweep produced.)

`sort -> orderBy` and `filters -> where` are alias-table entries, not typos: they are what a caller
who knows another query API reaches for, so edit distance cannot reach them. The same species as
the `visibleWhen -> visible` entry the #3746 template is built around. A key outside the table still
gets its name echoed plus a length-relative edit-distance suggestion (`ofset -> offset`), and an
unguessable one (`wibble`) gets the name and the history with no invented suggestion.

**A gap worth naming.** `packages/spec` has a compensating control for the same strip default — the
`authorable-surface/*.json` ratchet, whose own description says it exists "because these schemas are
not `.strict()` and Zod would silently strip it". `packages/mcp` had **neither**: zero `.strict()`
anywhere under `packages/mcp/src` at the branch point (positive control: the same matcher finds it
in `packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts` at the same commit), and zero ratchet shards naming it. The
#4001 campaign measured `packages/spec/src/**/*.zod.ts` and its per-directory table is spec's own
subdirectories, so this package was never inside that ratchet's scope. This is an **unextended
ratchet**, not a covered surface that was missed.

## Clause ② — declared from the delivered diff

Clause-②: no

Refusing keys that were never declared pulls real behaviour back onto the published text; it does
not narrow the text. The diff adds no key to any published payload, exports no new symbol, and
starts accepting no spelling it did not accept before — the alias table is used only to compose a
refusal message and is never parsed.

`Contract-text:` — the published contract for `query_records`, verbatim from
`packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts` at this branch's base commit `f8e57905`, where
`note('query_records')` sits at `:555` and the block below at `:560-573`. Coordinates in the card's
reports (`:465`) and in the dispatch (`:559-572` at `10da5c44`) have both moved again — derive them,
do not quote them:

```ts
        inputSchema: {
          objectName: z.string().describe('The object/table name'),
          where: z
            .record(z.string(), z.unknown())
            .optional()
            .describe('Filter conditions, e.g. {"status":"open"}'),
          fields: z.array(z.string()).optional().describe('Field names to return (defaults to all)'),
          limit: z.number().int().positive().max(maxLimit).optional().describe(`Max rows (≤ ${maxLimit})`),
          offset: z.number().int().nonnegative().optional().describe('Rows to skip'),
          orderBy: z
            .array(z.object({ field: z.string(), order: z.enum(['asc', 'desc']) }))
            .optional()
            .describe('Sort order'),
        },
```

Six keys are declared: `objectName`, `where`, `fields`, `limit`, `offset`, `orderBy`. `sort`,
`filters` and `filter` — the three spellings in the two repro reports — are absent from that list.

## Verification

- `packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.unknown-argument-keys.test.ts` — **6 failed / 4 passed at
  `a95cad3e`** (the test-only commit, before the fix), **10 passed** after. The 4 that were green
  throughout are the controls: the declared spellings reach the bridge, `{}` still works on an
  argument-less tool, eleven tools are advertised, and every tool accepts its declared arguments.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/mcp test` — 29 files / 313 tests pass; no pre-existing pin moved.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/mcp typecheck` — clean; the test-typecheck debt ledger held at
  6 files / 53 errors (no ratchet step).
- Both halves are pinned per route, as the repo requires: a refusal pin (refused **and** the bridge
  was never called) beside a preservation pin (the exact arguments the bridge received).
- **Gates: 59 path-derived families, all exit 0, 0 NOT MEASURED**, reconciled with
  `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --ran FILE` (exit codes
  captured before any pipe, per family). Three needed a full workspace build first
  (`check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:lean-entry-closure`, `check:type-check-debt` — each exits 3,
  which is NOT MEASURED rather than a pass); they were re-run green after
  `turbo run build --filter='./packages/*' --filter='./packages/*/*'` (72/72). `check:type-check-debt`
  additionally needs more than a 4 GB heap on a shared box.
- **`pnpm lint` — repo-scoped, exit 0.** Run whole, not narrowed, so no narrowing claim is needed.
- Measured at `0d6ed3fa`.

## Acceptance notes

- The `arguments`-omitted case (`tools/call` with no `arguments` member at all) already failed
  before this change and fails identically after — measured on both postures. Not touched here.
- #4134 records the same disease one layer down on REST list routes, failing toward empty where
  this one failed toward full. Noted only; no change here.

Left as **draft** for the maintainer to review and land.
